_comment: Single source of the quest_buttons mapping (FrameBridge adapter setting). Keys are Touch input names under /user/hand/<hand>/input/, values the Frame Controller inputs the binding is also suggested for. A button entry covers its bare path (e.g. input/x, which OpenXR resolves to click) and its click and touch components; menu covers the bare path and click only. native/adapter's table, tests/test_quest_buttons.py and scripts/controller_diagram.py follow this file. See docs/input/QUEST_BUTTONS.md.

0.name: SteamVR default
0.note: FrameBridge suggests nothing for the Frame profile; SteamVR remaps Touch itself (documented by Valve). Listed for the diagram only.

1.name: Mirror
1.note: Every face button works; the left controller mirrors the right: bottom + outer = X/A, top + inner = Y/B, as on Quest controllers.

2.name: Quest pair
2.note: Two buttons per controller, placed like Quest Touch's (the second one up and toward the other hand); the other face buttons do nothing.

3.name: One hand
3.note: All four Quest face buttons on the right controller, printed letter for letter (A, B, X, Y); the left d-pad also moves the left thumbstick; View is Menu.
3._other_hand: Touch input (key, on the hand named above it) <- the listed Frame inputs on the OTHER hand, click and touch. FrameBridge reads them through an action set of its own and answers the game's left X/Y actions (queried for the left hand or with no subaction path); no binding suggestion can do this (a right-hand binding feeds the right subaction).
3._dpad_stick: The hand's Touch thumbstick (vector and x/y) reads these d-pad buttons (up, down, left, right; click) as a direction while one is held; the real thumbstick otherwise. Diagonals are normalised to length 1.
